must_haves: Exactly ONE markdown notes editor component exists after this plan: frontend/src/components/NotesEditor.tsx. The old frontend/src/features/board/components/NotesEditor.tsx is deleted — grep -rn \"features/board/components/NotesEditor\" frontend/src returns zero hits and no second editor file defines a rehype-sanitize schema.

NotesEditor no longer imports useUpdateNotes or any board-feature hook; it saves exclusively through an onSave(notes: string) => Promise<unknown> | void prop, and its Save/Cancel disabled state + button label are driven by an isSaving: boolean prop (not update.isPending).

The hardened SANITIZE_SCHEMA (defaultSchema minus script/iframe/object/embed) is preserved byte-for-byte — the markdown sanitization applied in Preview is identical to the pre-move board behavior; no schema field is added, removed, or reordered.
On a resolved onSave the editor switches to the Preview tab; on a rejected onSave it stays on Edit (mirrors the prior onSuccess-only setTab('preview') behavior exactly).

CardDetailModal imports NotesEditor from '@/components/NotesEditor', owns its own const updateNotes = useUpdateNotes(), and passes onSave={(notes) => updateNotes.mutateAsync({ cardId: card.id, notes })} + isSaving={updateNotes.isPending}; the board card notes still save, still optimistically update, and still flip to Preview on success.

The generalized props are: initialNotes: string; notesUpdatedAt: string | null; notesUpdatedBy: string | null (a pre-resolved display name or null — component never resolves ids); onSave; isSaving; resetKey?: string. The draft-reset effect depends on [resetKey, initialNotes] so switching entities with identical notes still resets a dirty draft; CardDetailModal passes resetKey={card.id}.
